summary: This lecture tells of the Second Pledge of Aqabah, the point of no return in the Prophet's ﷺ sirah. The ustaz recalls Mus'ab ibn Umayr's da'wah in Yathrib, then explains how the Yathrib hajj caravan, including about 75 Muslims, planned a secret meeting with the Prophet on the last night of the days of tashriq. Drawing on the hadiths of Ka'b ibn Malik and Jabir ibn Abdullah, he tells of their first meeting with the Prophet, Al-Abbas's speech, the terms of the pledge, Abul Haitham's pointed question, As'ad ibn Zurarah's warning about the risk, the appointment of twelve naqibs, the shout of Satan and the Quraysh's investigation the next day. The ustaz closes with ten lessons from the episode and ends the second season with a recommended Tadabbur Juz 'Amma book and an outline of season three on the Hijrah.
keyPoints: The Second Pledge of Aqabah was the point of no return, when the Prophet ﷺ and the Ansar bound themselves to full protection despite the risk of war.
The Ansar did not ask what they would get in worldly terms but thought of the Prophet's ﷺ protection, and the reward they asked for was Paradise.
The pledge was kept secret with great care on the last night of hajj, and only about 15 percent of the Yathrib group knew.
The Prophet ﷺ explained the terms transparently and eased Abul Haitham's worry by saying their blood was one and he would not leave them.
When invited to attack Mina, the Prophet ﷺ answered that they had not been commanded to do so and told them to return to their tents.
The second season ends and the third will begin with the Hijrah.

chapters.title: Opening: the morning dua and the fitrah
chapters.summary: The ustaz begins with the morning dua on the fitrah of Islam and the word of sincerity.

chapters.title: Point of no return and Mus'ab's work in Yathrib
chapters.summary: Episode 47 is the tipping point, recalling the da'wah of Mus'ab ibn Umayr and Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, which reached every household.

chapters.title: The Yathrib hajj group of the 13th year
chapters.summary: About 500 people set out from Yathrib with 75 Muslims, and Jabir's hadith tells of ten years of the Prophet offering himself without result.

chapters.title: The Ansar's question and the secret meeting
chapters.summary: The Ansar thought of the Prophet's ﷺ interests, not their own, and arranged a secret meeting on the last night of the days of tashriq.

chapters.title: Ka'b ibn Malik, Al-Bara' and the dispute over the qiblah
chapters.summary: On the way to Makkah, Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur wished to pray facing the Ka'bah while the others kept facing Syria.

chapters.title: Meeting the Prophet for the first time
chapters.summary: They asked Al-Abbas and met the Prophet ﷺ, who recognised Ka'b as the poet before answering the qiblah question.

chapters.title: The secret preparations and Abu Jabir
chapters.summary: They slipped out like sand grouse, Abu Jabir embraced Islam at the last moment, and two women also attended.

chapters.title: Al-Abbas's speech
chapters.summary: Al-Abbas, still not a Muslim, tested the Ansar's resolve and warned of the responsibility of protecting the Prophet.

chapters.title: The terms of the pledge and Abul Haitham's question
chapters.summary: The Prophet listed the terms of tawhid, shelter and protection, and Abul Haitham asked whether he would leave them after victory.

chapters.title: As'ad ibn Zurarah's warning and the pledge
chapters.summary: As'ad stressed the risk of the pledge, and they refused to withdraw and pledged one by one.

chapters.title: The twelve naqibs
chapters.summary: The Prophet asked them to choose twelve leaders themselves, nine from Khazraj and three from Aws.

chapters.title: The shout of Satan and the Prophet stopping a fight
chapters.summary: Satan shouted the news of the pledge, and when Al-Abbas ibn Ubadah offered to attack Mina the Prophet refused and sent them back to their tents.

chapters.title: The Quraysh question them and the new-shoes ruse
chapters.summary: Quraysh leaders investigated the Khazraj tents, the Muslims kept the secret, and Sa'd ibn Ubadah was captured but released.

chapters.title: Ten lessons
chapters.summary: Mature faith, appreciation, respect for differences and the sunnah, da'wah to the end, transparency about risk, an open exit, difficult conversations, shura, knowledge over emotion and Paradise as the goal.

chapters.title: Closing the second season and book recommendation
chapters.summary: This is the last episode of season two, with a long break, a recommended Tadabbur Juz 'Amma book and an outline of season three beginning with the Hijrah.

dalil.context: The ustaz says he offered this for ten years without result before the Ansar accepted it.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah ten years approaching people at their stopping places, in the markets and in the hajj season, saying: who will protect me and help me convey my Lord's message, for him is Paradise.

dalil.context: They thought of the Prophet's interests, not what they would get.
dalil.translation: So seventy men of us set out until we reached him in the hajj season.

dalil.context: Linked to the Ansar who longed for the Prophet though they had never seen his face.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said I long for my brothers. When the Companions asked if they were his brothers, he replied you are my companions; my brothers are those who never saw me yet believe in me.

dalil.context: The ustaz gives two readings: stay on the original qiblah, or a hint that another qiblah was coming but it was not yet time.
dalil.translation: The Prophet answered Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur: you were on a qiblah, had you been patient with it, and Al-Bara' returned to praying toward Syria with the Prophet.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this hadith is weak but not fabricated, and its details match stronger hadiths.
dalil.translation: The Prophet asked the Ansar to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him, to give him and his Companions shelter, and to protect them as they protect themselves, and their reward is Paradise.

dalil.context: This is a total commitment that does not depend on emotion or finances.
dalil.translation: Pledge to me to listen and obey in energy and in sluggishness, to spend in hardship and ease, to enjoin good and forbid evil, to speak the truth for Allah without fearing blame, and to help and protect me as you protect yourselves, your wives and children, and for you is Paradise.

dalil.context: The Prophet's answer to Abul Haitham, who feared he would leave them after victory, words the ustaz says deserve framing.
dalil.translation: Your blood is my blood, your ruin is my ruin; I am of you and you are of me. I fight whom you fight and make peace with whom you make peace.

dalil.context: The Prophet said it later at Hunayn, showing this pledge made them one.
dalil.translation: Were it not for the Hijrah, I would be one of the Ansar.

dalil.context: The two women who attended took the pledge verbally.
dalil.translation: Aisha RA relates that the Prophet took the women's pledge by word, and never touched the hand of any woman except one lawful to him.

dalil.context: The Muslims only exchanged glances without speaking.
dalil.translation: The next morning Quraysh leaders came to the tents and said word has reached us that you pledged to take our companion out and fight us. The polytheists of Yathrib swore nothing happened and spoke truly because they did not know.

dalil.context: Ka'b took a good omen from the new shoes given by Al-Harith.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ liked good omens (fa'l), meaning positive words about the future.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions three phrases: thank you, sorry and please.
dalil.translation: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.

dalil.context: Surah al-Hujurat warns believers not to put themselves ahead of Allah and His Messenger, like Al-Bara' accepting the Prophet's answer. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Believers, do not push yourselves forward in the presence of God and His Messenger––be mindful of God: He hears and knows all––

people.context: In one year made almost every household in Yathrib have a believer, and returned with a report before the hajj of the 13th year.
Sent with Mus'ab; the ustaz likens Mus'ab to the marketer and him to the teacher.
Narrator of the hadith on the Prophet offering himself for ten years and the trip to Aqabah, and Al-Bara's nephew.

people.role: Leader of the group and Ansar spokesman
people.context: The youngest and most prominent that night, Mus'ab's host, who warned of the risk before the pledge.

people.role: Leader of Yathrib and later chief of the hypocrites
people.context: Was in the group but did not know what was planned.
Narrator of the long hadith about this night, later tested with a 50-day boycott, and became a poet of the Prophet.
Did not return Ka'b's greeting during the 50-day boycott despite their closeness.
Prayed facing the Ka'bah on the way, returned to the Prophet's qiblah, and may have been the first to pledge. He died before the Prophet reached Madinah and bequeathed a third of his wealth.
Guarded the lanes and signalled if anyone approached during the secret meeting.
Embraced Islam at the last moment, attended that night and was appointed naqib, later dying a martyr at Uhud.
One of the two women who attended the Second Aqabah.
The second woman who attended the Second Aqabah.
Not yet a Muslim but attended and opened the speeches to ensure the Ansar were serious.
Asked whether the Prophet would leave them after victory if they cut their pact with the Jews.
Narrated that the Prophet took the women's pledge verbally.
The richest of the Ansar, later paired with Abdurrahman ibn Auf.
An important Companion praised by the Prophet and later a military commander.
Once came to drive Mus'ab out of Yathrib on Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's orders.
Came in new shoes that became a ruse to distract, then embraced Islam at the Conquest of Makkah and died a martyr in Syria.
Captured and beaten by Quraysh on the way home but released because he had protected Makkan merchants.

lessons.title: Mature faith asks what it can give
lessons.body: Unlike a transactional mindset, the Prophet and Companions always thought about what they could contribute to the religion.

lessons.title: Small talk and appreciation build loyalty
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ said 'al-sha'ir' to Ka'b, a small gesture that won his heart, and Ka'b became a poet of the Prophet.

lessons.title: Thank you, sorry and please
lessons.body: These three simple phrases make people comfortable near us, and not thanking people means not thanking Allah.

lessons.title: Respect differences in ijtihad and put the sunnah first
lessons.body: Differences of opinion are unavoidable in fiqh and respected when based on facts and evidence, aiming at the spirit of the sunnah.

lessons.title: Submit when the Prophet's guidance arrives
lessons.body: Al-Bara' did not argue when the Prophet answered, and we should not seek loopholes to depart from the hadith.

lessons.title: Call to the very last moment
lessons.body: Abu Jabir was invited to Islam hours before the pledge, since da'wah rules no one out and is done with empathy.

lessons.title: Da'wah wins hearts, not arguments
lessons.body: The core of da'wah is winning hearts, not defeating the person being called.

lessons.title: Be transparent about risk
lessons.body: All parties should be clear about the terms and risks of an agreement, with no hidden clauses, so that trust is built.

lessons.title: Give an exit before the door is locked
lessons.body: Those unable to bear a commitment are given a chance to withdraw, not forced or guilt-tripped.

lessons.title: Face difficult conversations with a smile
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ smiled and answered Abul Haitham's blunt question calmly, not offended.

lessons.title: Create psychological safety and shura
lessons.body: The Prophet received and engaged differing views with a smile, valued shura, and let the people of Madinah choose their own leaders.

lessons.title: Zeal must be guided by knowledge, not emotion
lessons.body: Many study circles and da'wah activities should make us more rational and wise, not merely emotional.

lessons.title: Paradise as the ultimate goal
lessons.body: The Ansar said they took the pledge for Paradise, so ask how far Paradise motivates our own lives.

lessons.title: The Prophet rejected the shortcut of violence
lessons.body: When offered an attack on a sleeping Mina, the Prophet ﷺ replied that they had not been commanded to do so.

lessons.title: A person's quality is not measured by length of Islam
lessons.body: Abu Jabir had been Muslim only hours yet was made naqib, because what matters is a heart on the truth.

glossary.meaning: A pledge of allegiance and a pact taken by placing a hand in the leader's hand.
Helpers: the people of Madinah who supported the Prophet.
The 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah after Eid al-Adha.
The stoning site at Mina near the first jamrah, location of the secret pact.
A chief or person in charge of a people, like a sub-commander in the Aqabah pledge.
Another name for the Second Pledge of Aqabah, the pledge of war.
The Companions who migrated from Makkah to Madinah.
Good words or omens about the future, which the Prophet liked.
